title: How G-12 becomes a trusted reference case
introduction: Illustrative team workflow; adapt responsibilities and criteria. Follow one fictional row from an unlabeled candidate to a versioned regression reference. A “golden” label describes reviewed reference data for a stated use, not universal certification or proof that a model is good.
policy: Fictional handbook RE-7 revision 1: “One pause per 12 months; maximum 30 days; an adviser must confirm eligibility.” Rubric R1: a request outside any policy limit requires referral and must not promise approval.
question: G-12: “I used a 20-day pause four months ago. Can I take another 10 days now?”

stages.title: Agree what the reference set covers
stages.action: Limit this reference set to pause-policy questions. The policy owner confirms RE-7 revision 1 and rubric R1. The evaluation engineer defines the labels and the test role.
stages.before:
Dataset scope = undecided
Allowed answer authority = unknown
stages.after:
Scope = pause eligibility under RE-7 revision 1
Labels = referral-required | adviser-confirmation-required
Use = reviewed regression reference; no automatic eligibility approval
stages.artifact: Scope record S1: policy owner, RE-7 revision 1, rubric R1, intended use and excluded tasks.
stages.gate: The policy owner confirms the source and rubric. The PM records the intended use; labels never authorize a customer action.
stages.blocked: If nobody can confirm RE-7 authority, stop here. Do not let a convenient model answer define the policy.

stages.title: Record a candidate case
stages.action: Maya supplies the fictional question. The data steward preserves the four-month interval and 20-day history, records provenance and checks that no customer details are present.
stages.after:
G-12
question = “I used a 20-day pause four months ago. Can I take another 10 days now?”
source = RE-7 revision 1
provenance = fictional adviser scenario
expected = unset
split = unassigned
status = candidate
stages.artifact: Candidate record G-12 with source text, fictional provenance and a stable ID.
stages.gate: The row has enough facts to apply the rule, a permitted source and no unnecessary personal data. It has no trusted label yet.
stages.blocked: If the earlier pause date is missing, return to Maya for the fact. If source authority is unknown, return to scope.

stages.title: Collect independent labels
stages.action: Give both reviewers G-12, RE-7 and R1. Hide each reviewer’s label until both submit. Preserve their labels and reasons verbatim.
stages.after:
Maya.label = answer-yes
Maya.reason = “20 + 10 = 30 days, so 10 remain.”
Leila.label = referral-required
Leila.reason = “A previous pause four months ago breaches one pause per 12 months.”
resolved = unset
stages.artifact: Two review records attached to G-12; reviewer identity, source revision, rubric revision and each reason remain visible.
stages.gate: Both reviewers submit without seeing the other label. answer-yes is retained as Maya’s raw response even though R1 does not permit it.
stages.blocked: One reviewer copying the other is not independent review. Obtain another independent review; do not fabricate agreement.

stages.title: Hold the disagreement open
stages.action: Flag the exact conflict: Maya treats 30 days as a balance; Leila applies the one-pause limit. Send both reasons, the policy and the rubric for adjudication.
stages.after:
G-12.status = disputed
conflict = reusable day balance versus one pause per 12 months
Maya = answer-yes
Leila = referral-required
resolved = unset
scoring = blocked
stages.artifact: Disagreement record D12 links both original reviews to the same RE-7 revision 1 clause.
stages.gate: The adjudicator can inspect the actual source, facts and rubric. A majority vote or model preference does not settle policy authority.
stages.blocked: Do not silently take the first label or discard the row. If the source is genuinely ambiguous, return to the policy owner at scope.

stages.title: Resolve against policy and rubric
stages.action: Apply both RE-7 limits. The prior pause was four months ago, so the one-pause rule is breached even though 20 + 10 = 30. Record the resolved label and an acceptable draft.
stages.before:
G-12.status = disputed
Maya = answer-yes
Leila = referral-required
resolved = unset
stages.after:
G-12.status = adjudicated
original labels = Maya: answer-yes; Leila: referral-required
resolved = referral-required
reason = prior pause four months ago breaches one pause per 12 months
expected draft = “RE-7 allows one pause per 12 months. Your earlier pause was four months ago, so another pause is outside this rule. An adviser must review your eligibility; I cannot approve a second pause.”
stages.artifact: Adjudication A12 records the source clause, rubric R1, resolution and expected answer. Neither original label is overwritten.
stages.gate: The policy owner accepts the interpretation. The expected answer mentions the 12-month limit, the four-month fact and RE-7; it makes no approval promise.
stages.blocked: If the expected draft says “you have 10 days left”, return to dispute. If RE-7 cannot settle it, seek a policy decision rather than inventing an answer.

stages.title: Validate labels and control the split
stages.collaborator: Data steward and independent label reviewer
stages.action: An independent reviewer checks A12 against RE-7 and R1. QA checks required fields, duplicates, preserved labels and the scoring check. The data steward records that G-12 has been exposed to the team.
stages.before:
G-12.status = adjudicated
split = unassigned
scorer check = untested
stages.after:
G-12.status = validated
split = regression (already discussed and exposed)
label audit = referral-required agrees with RE-7/R1
original reviews = retained
positive control = expected draft passes
negative control = “Yes, you have 10 days left” fails
stages.artifact: Validation V12 contains label-review result, duplicate/group check, split assignment and positive/negative scorer outputs.
stages.gate: All required checks pass. Keep related cases in one split. Reserve separately collected, unseen cases for the release holdout; G-12 cannot become untouched again.
stages.blocked: If the wrong 10-day-balance answer passes, fix the scorer before proceeding. If policy checking disagrees, return to adjudication; if facts are incomplete, return to candidate.

stages.title: Freeze a versioned reference
stages.action: Publish reference-set version pause-regression-v1 with G-12, RE-7 revision 1, R1 and the validation record. Store an immutable manifest or checksum and a separate place for run results.
stages.before:
Validated working copy
G-12.resolved = referral-required
split = regression
stages.after:
reference version = pause-regression-v1
G-12 source = RE-7 revision 1
G-12 resolved = referral-required
G-12 split = regression
reviews + A12 + V12 = retained
model result = not yet measured
stages.artifact: Frozen reference manifest binds rows, source/rubric revisions, split and review records. A model run records its own model/prompt versions and results.
stages.gate: The dataset owner accepts the reference’s intended use and limits after QA passes. “Frozen” means a stable comparison reference; it does not prove model quality or authorize release.
stages.blocked: Do not edit G-12 inside v1 after a run. A label defect or policy update opens a new working version and preserves the old reference.

stages.title: Reopen after policy or evidence changes
stages.collaborator: Policy owner, data steward and QA
stages.action: The policy owner publishes fictional RE-7 revision 2: up to two pauses per 12 months, combined maximum 30 days; an adviser must confirm eligibility. Reopen G-12 in a new working version for independent review.
stages.before:
pause-regression-v1 remains frozen
RE-7 revision 1 = one pause per 12 months
G-12 resolved = referral-required
stages.after:
pause-regression-v2 draft
source = RE-7 revision 2: “Up to two pauses per 12 months; combined maximum 30 days; an adviser must confirm eligibility.”
question = unchanged
prior 1 pause + proposed 1 = 2; 20 + 10 = 30 days
proposed label = adviser-confirmation-required
resolved = unset pending independent review
old v1 resolution = preserved
stages.artifact: Change record C12 identifies the changed clause, affected row and new draft. The proposed label is not an approved customer action or a finished reference.
stages.gate: Validate source authority and applicability, then repeat independent labels, adjudication if needed, QA and freeze. The expected draft may say the numeric limits fit, but must still require adviser confirmation.
stages.blocked: Never silently relabel historical runs against revision 2. If applicability is unknown, return to scope. Keep revision 1 results tied to revision 1.
